author: agent
text:
DEFECT found by eye on 2026-08-16, not by any test: the browser tab of EVERY map memway generates reads "memway - itsdangerous, the real map". The title is hardcoded at viz_template.html:6 and export() never overrides it, so it is not a memway.io problem - it ships in the wheel and every user's map claims to be a map of itsdangerous. Verified on maps built by the published 0.54.0 wheel for two unrelated repos: both carry that title, and on the live memway.io/map.html the string "itsdangerous" appears EXACTLY ONCE in 761KB - only in the title - while the body is memway's own 909 entities.

It is a leftover from the registry-demo era, when the flagship map really was itsdangerous. Nothing caught it because the title is a constant, not behaviour: the payload tests, the airgap tests and the executed-predicate tests all pass on a page whose tab lies. This is the same class as the dead lens toggle and the copyable-block placement - three of the last five user-visible defects were invisible to every automated layer and were found by a human looking at the screen.

Second, related defect on the same surface: the header label is f"{repo_p.name}..." (viz.py:227), the DIRECTORY name, so memway's own flagship map is published reading "coordsys-v49" - the pre-rename directory. A project name should come from pyproject/package.json/git remote and fall back to the directory, never lead with it.

Wanted: title derived from the same source as the header, so a map cannot advertise a repo it does not describe, plus a test asserting the emitted title contains the repo label and does NOT contain a hardcoded project name.
